scenes.narration: This coin is fair. But your chance of winning this game is not one half. Start with two tokens. Heads adds one. Tails takes one away. Reach six tokens and you win. Reach zero and the game ends. Every toss is fifty fifty, but you start much closer to losing. What is the actual chance of reaching six first? Instead of guessing, give each position a height: its chance of eventually winning. Zero tokens means zero chance. Six tokens means certainty. What height belongs to the positions between them? From any middle position, the next fair toss moves you one step left or one step right. Your current winning chance must therefore be the average of those two neighbors. Look at the heights. Each middle dot must sit exactly halfway between the dots beside it. That forces equal steps all the way across. From zero chance to full certainty, divided into six equal steps. Starting at two tokens puts you two steps up: two sixths, or one third. The little game board and the probability picture are describing the same starting position. Move the start to three tokens. Now you are halfway between the boundaries, so the chance really is one half. Start at five, and it is five sixths. A fair toss tells us the next step is balanced. It does not tell us two unequal journeys are equally likely. The distance to the finish matters.
